title: Living Blueprint machine (app/machine.json)
description: The single data spine behind /blueprint/: what exists, when it arrived, what it unlocked, and who it powers — and nothing about how it looks. The renderer owns every pixel; this file owns every claim. Honesty invariants beyond this schema live in scripts/check-machine.py (make machine-check). Pattern: docs/patterns/living-blueprint.md.

changelog.description: Newest first. Bump version+updated+changelog together on every edit (fill-in envelope convention).

views.description: The layer views: same silhouette, different splits. Keys are view ids (slugs); each view defines the ordered groups a component may belong to in that view. Group membership drives layout/regrouping; geometry identity never changes between views.

phaseRef.description: Must match the id of an entry in timeline.phases (validator V4/V1). Engagements name their own phases; special rendering behaviors come from the phase definition's `kind`, never from magic ids.

order.description: Band/stack order within the view (0 = first).

ref.description: A tracker item: Jira-style KEY-123 or GitHub-style #123.
A decision id; resolved against app/decisions.json ids when that file exists (validator V5).

date.description: Real delivery date (tracker done-date). Required when built.

sequence.description: Tie-break for colorization order when components share a delivery date: lower colorizes first.

gated.description: Built but activation-gated: colorizes at its build date — the one deliberate legend exception, never ghosted — and carries an activation label ('built <phase> · activated <activationPhase>'). Requires activationPhase.

feedCadence.description: How fast, and in what shape, data arrives on an ingestion channel. The ONLY source of flow animation rate: the renderer reads mode + ratePerMin and never hardcodes a per-channel speed. Rate drives density (spawn interval, dash-march), never velocity — 'speed is time-scale, density is volume' (blueprint/design/motion-language.md).

mode.description: Arrival shape: burst = clustered trains between idle gaps (batch pulls) · continuous = evenly spaced trickle (webhooks, streams, CDC) · scheduled = one discrete arrival per interval (file drops). Usual pairings with channelType, not enforced ones.

ratePerMin.description: Average records per minute over the channel's own cycle. 0 = provisioned but not yet fed: the route draws live and empty.

officialName.description: PRIMARY display name, in the engagement's real spec/portal vocabulary. What every renderer shows by default, in every view, at every depth. Not an invented coinage, not a vendor/product name.

metaphorName.description: OPTIONAL visual-metaphor flavor name (see blueprint/design/metaphor-dictionary.md). Never replaces officialName; at most a secondary/subtitle line. Must not contain any realName token (validator V7).

realName.description: Engineer-depth name; vendor and product names allowed here. Its tokens (minus officialName's) form the V7 denylist for exec surfaces.

execCopy.description: The card's what-it-does body: one sentence, capability language, no technology names (V7).

valueLine.description: The card's why-it-matters line: one line of value language (V7 applies). Must not restate execCopy in different words — that is a review failure no schema can catch.

engCopy.description: Optional engineer-depth description; tech names allowed.

deepLink.description: Engineer-mode link (repo path, portal page, dashboard). Never shown at exec depth.

specRef.description: Optional plan-node id in specs/manifest.json whose status this component's delivery tracks; scripts/sync-machine.py refreshes delivery from it (make machine-sync).

handlesPii.description: True if raw PII/sensitive data transits or rests here. Drives validator V6 on connections.

existing.description: True for systems that predate the project: colorized from timeline start at every scrub position.

channelType.description: INGESTION-CHANNEL COMPONENTS ONLY — the intake form this channel takes and the typed flow it feeds. Omit on non-intake components. Present ⇒ feedCadence required.

views.description: Membership per layer view: key = a view id defined at top level, value = a group id defined in that view. Key present = component appears in that view.

slot.description: Optional named geometry slot — the bridge to hand-drawn frame art (slice 2 of the design spec). Absent components render as auto-laid-out placeholder blocks; no coordinates ever live in this file.

internals.description: Sub-parts revealed at detail depth (slice 2 explode). Frame-local; authored without knowledge of placement.

flow.description: stream = continuous flow · batch = scheduled runs · request = call/response · reference = lookup/read-only.

pii.description: True if untokenized PII/sensitive data travels this path. Both endpoints must declare handlesPii (V6).

label.description: Exec-safe payload label ('customer records', 'events'). No tech names (V7).

delivery.description: Optional override. If absent, derived: built iff both endpoints built (date = later endpoint date); else the least-advanced endpoint status.

name.description: Capability language; leads every exec surface (V7).

body.description: What it does, stated directly — no before/after scaffold. For planned capabilities the renderer casts this in future tense; the copy stays declarative.

valueLine.description: Why it matters, one line of value language. Not a restatement of body.

problem.description: The business problem this addresses. Pure value language: no names, no meeting attribution.

problemRef.description: Optional stable id of a canonical problem statement; verbatim text lives in `problem`, attribution stripped.

products.description: CANONICAL capability→product edge. Product cards derive their consumed-capabilities list by inverting this; the edge is stored exactly once.

status.description: The ASSESSED STATUS ONCE UNLOCKED — what the capability honestly claims when its machinery is built (done AND usable in a live environment). Optional and IGNORED while the card is locked: until at least one unlockedBy component is built, the renderer suppresses the chip entirely (V3c).

statusNote.description: Required when status is present and != 'solves' (V3b): what is partial, or what unblocks it.

unlockedBy.description: ALL listed components must be built for the capability to unlock at a timeline position (V3).

name.description: The downstream product/consumer this machine powers.

beat.description: Ordinal within the scenario. Pacing/duration is presentation, not data.

action.description: Closed 14-verb vocabulary — the single source of truth for the beat player. New verbs require a schema version bump.

target.description: Component id (arrive/process/split/merge/hold/divert/emit/deliver), connection id (travel), component|connection id (flag/camera), component|capability id (card). Optional anchor for caption; absent for wait. Enforced by V2a.

payload.description: Exec-safe token label carried through the machine. No tech names (V7).

execIntro.description: The problem this walkthrough answers, in value language. No attribution.

demonstrates.description: Capability ids this scenario proves out.

timeline.description: Scrub positions are DERIVED from component delivery dates — never hand-listed. This object holds only the fixed frame: phase windows and named markers.

start.description: Required for delivery-kind phases (the V4 window); optional for reference/unnumbered, which have no window.

kind.description: delivery (default) = normal phase, dates checked against the window (V4). reference = machinery outside the delivery timeline: reference treatment, never colorizes, exempt from V4. unnumbered = deliberately un-dated later work ('a later phase'): ghosted, rendered without a numeral, exempt from V4.
